title: Policy adjudicator for dedicated vs hosted routing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a centralized policy adjudicator service that determines routing decisions between Dedicated capacity and Hosted spillover. The adjudicator evaluates multi-dimensional inputs (tenant tier, region affinity, dedicated headroom, current latency SLI, per-request model variant compatibility, and cost delta thresholds) and emits deterministic routing outcomes (route to dedicated, route to hosted, demote to cheaper model variant, or queue/grace-window). Goal: make failover predictable, SLO-first, and reversible while minimizing cost impact and noisy oscillations during bursts. This ticket covers the decision matrix, safety controls (circuit-breakers, cooldown windows, soft-reserve lanes), API contract for the router, a canary rollout plan, and instrumentation to validate customer-visible behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Adjudicator API spec (gRPC/HTTP) reviewed and merged with request/response schema that includes reason codes and telemetry tags
A decision matrix implemented that covers tenant tiers (free, standard, enterprise), region affinity (same-region, cross-region), and three capacity states (healthy, low-headroom, degraded)
Unit + integration tests for policy logic with mocked capacity and SLI inputs covering >95% branches
End-to-end canary showing 0 regression in P95 latency for enterprise tenants during a controlled hosted spill scenario
Dashboard widgets showing routing decisions, decision reasons breakdown, and per-tenant cost delta estimates
Runbook with playbook steps for reverting policy changes and manual override endpoints documented
decisions: SLO-first: If dedicated latency SLO is currently failing for a tenant, route to hosted only if hosted model variant meets tenant quality threshold
Soft-reserve: Enterprise tier receives a configurable soft-reserve of connections (logical slots) for 30s grace window before preemption
Model-demote threshold: Only demote to cheaper quantized variant if historical eval score delta <= configurable threshold (default 0.03 QA metric)
Cost-aware tie-breaker: When both dedicated and hosted are healthy, prefer dedicated for enterprise and prefer hosted for free tier when cost delta > 20%
risks: Oscillation: aggressive short windows could cause flip-flopping between dedicated and hosted and increase overall latency
Quality regressions: model variant demotion could produce user-visible quality drops if thresholds misconfigured
Capacity storms: simultaneous preemption of many tenants might swamp hosted capacity and trigger cascading failures
Data skew: regional headroom signals might be stale leading to suboptimal routing decisions
implementation_steps: 1) Draft decision matrix and reason codes (this doc).
2) Define adjudicator API and protobufs; add to internal service registry.
3) Implement core decision engine in Go with pluggable input adapters (telemetry, capacity cache, model capability registry).
4) Add local simulator harness to replay historical traffic traces against policy rules.
5) Integrate with router: small synchronous check with timeout fallback to existing router logic.
6) Build basic dashboard panels and expose reason-code metrics and histograms.
7) Run canary for a subset of tenants (10% of enterprise, 5% of standard) with extended tracing.
8) Iterate on thresholds and add automated rollback triggers based on SLO regressions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for every rule and edge case
Integration test with router that exercises timeout and fallback paths
Replay tests using last 30 days of routing traces with injected host/region outages
Canary: staged rollout with synthetic traffic spikes and manual verification of cost/latency metrics
Chaos test: introduce artificial capacity loss in a region and verify adjudicator stabilizes routing within configured grace period
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: adjudicator.decision.count{reason,tenant_tier} emitted to metrics backend
New SLO alert: if canary enterprise P95 latency increases >5% relative to baseline for >5m, auto-disable policy and alert oncall
Dashboard: per-region headroom + host spill ratio + model-demote rate
Alert: rapid oscillation (>=10 decision flips per tenant in 2 minutes) triggers pager
